item.title: #3123401: Stop caching route lookups with query parameters or without results
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 5 files, +45/−33 · php +40/−30 · yml +3/−3 · sql +2
  • Diff: 9f63dc7
  • Discussion: #3123401 · 15 contributors · 57 comments
  • Followers: 25
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 15 contributors

Summary

The route lookup cache no longer stores entries for requests that have a query string, and no longer stores lookups that find no route (404s). Previously every distinct path plus query string combination created its own cache entry. Those entries were all invalidated at once by the single route_match tag whenever a path alias changed, so hit rates on busy sites were low and the cache could fill with entries that were never reused. Requests for plain paths that resolve to a route are cached as before. Lookups with query strings now run the route and path alias queries each time, so sites may see a few extra queries on those requests.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • New API: New protected RouteProvider::useRouteCache(Request $request): bool, which subclasses can override to control whether a route lookup is cached.

Technical details

RouteProvider::getRouteCollectionForRequest() now computes the cache ID only when the new protected method useRouteCache() returns TRUE. By default that is $request->query->count() === 0. When it returns FALSE, the cache get() is skipped as well as the set(). The lookup is also only written to the cache when the resulting collection has routes or resources, so empty (404) results are never stored. The FALSE handling for previously cached empty results on the read path is unchanged, so existing entries are still read.

The cache ID logic and the route_match cache tag are untouched. Further improvements are tracked in #3621551. The original report was about empty results being cached with insufficient context (for example language or domain). Maintainers could not reproduce a routing-level cause, and the change was reframed as a performance task. Alternatives discussed included removing the cache entirely and adding cache contexts to the 404 lookup (#3580545). Tests updated: testRouteCaching() now asserts no cache entry for query-string and non-existing paths, PathWorkspacesTest::testPathAliasesWithTranslation() assertions changed, and the performance test fixtures (query and cache get counts, including the standard login flow) were adjusted.

Upgrade

Code that asserts or relies on route: cache entries for query-string or 404 requests will no longer find them. A subclass that wants different behavior can override the new method:

protected function useRouteCache(Request $request): bool {
  return $request->query->count() === 0;
}

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 30, 2020
  • Committed: November 27, 2026 (6 years later)

Key contributors

  • kadiiski
  • leoleoasd
  • drclaw (Fuse Interactive)
  • catch (Tag1 Consulting)
  • berdir (MD Systems GmbH)
  • scott_euser (Soapbox)

Collaboration

Berdir profiled the route cache on Umami with Blackfire and xhprof. He found that most of the cost on a miss was the cache write, and that the hit rate on active sites was poor. He first built an experimental MR that removed the cache entirely, then narrowed the change after catch said he preferred only skipping lookups with query strings and those with no results. Scott Euser tested manually on a standard install. He confirmed that four page visits left 16 route cache entries before the change and 2 after, and that creating an alias for a former 404 path worked straight away.

item.title: #3641618: Update Symfony
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +134/−131 · lock +119/−116 · json +15/−15
  • Diff: 270f520
  • Discussion: #3641618 · 3 contributors · 20 comments
  • Followers: 5
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 3 contributors

Summary

Drupal core's locked Symfony packages were updated in response to multiple Symfony CVEs announced on 2026-11-25. The fixes are in Symfony patch releases, so sites can pick them up by updating Symfony with Composer without waiting for a Drupal core release. The same update was committed to all seven branches: 10.6.x, 11.3.x, 11.4.x, 11.5.x, 11.x, 12.0.x and main.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: Updates Symfony packages to releases fixing multiple CVEs announced 2026-11-25; the issue does not detail severity.

Technical details

The commit shown here, on main, changes composer.lock only (the diff contains no other files). It moves the Symfony 8.2 packages (for example symfony/console, symfony/http-foundation, symfony/http-kernel, symfony/routing, symfony/validator, symfony/yaml) from v8.2.0-BETA1/v8.2.0-BETA2 to v8.2.0-RC1. The issue's lock diffs for the other branches list the following: 10.6.x moves to Symfony 6.4.49 through 6.4.51 packages; 11.3.x, 11.4.x, 11.5.x and 11.x move to 7.4.17 through 7.4.24 packages. Several of the 6.4 and 7.4 branches also move the symfony/*-contracts packages to v3.8.1 and the Symfony polyfills.

A comment on the issue notes that 12.0.x and main have to stay on beta compatibility in ComposerProjectTemplatesTest, because not every Symfony package has an 8.2 RC yet. The issue does not name the individual CVEs.

Upgrade

Sites that do not want to wait for a core release can update Symfony directly, for example:

composer update "symfony/*" --with-all-dependencies

  • Committed: November 26, 2026 (1 day later)

item.title: #3622582: Cleanup database exceptions
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Critical task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 44 files, +528/−122 · php +528/−122
  • Diff: 3de62ec
  • Discussion: #3622582 · 8 contributors · 43 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 2 of 8 contributors

Summary

The database exception classes were reorganized so that errors coming from the database client are all subclasses of DatabaseExceptionWrapper, and every exception implements the DatabaseException interface. Missing and already existing tables now throw dedicated exceptions. Exception messages now show the SQL and its placeholder values on a single line, instead of a multi-line print_r() dump.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • API change: Exception hierarchy changed, DatabaseExceptionWrapper gets an optional $info argument, SchemaDefinitionException no longer extends SchemaException, and Connection::getDriverClass() throws \InvalidArgumentException.
  • Deprecation: TransactionExplicitCommitNotAllowedException is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 with no replacement.
  • New API: New SqlExecutionInfo, SchemaTableDoesNotExistException and SchemaTableAlreadyExistsException.

Technical details

DatabaseExceptionWrapper now takes an optional fourth constructor argument, a public readonly ?SqlExecutionInfo $info. The new SqlExecutionInfo value object holds sqlQuery, placeholders and options. Its toCompactString() collapses whitespace in the query and escapes newlines in string placeholder values. appendToMessage() builds the message suffix : <sql>; [name=value, ...].

Inheritance changes: IntegrityConstraintViolationException, DatabaseAccessDeniedException, DatabaseConnectionRefusedException, DatabaseNotFoundException, SchemaException and TransactionException now extend DatabaseExceptionWrapper. ConnectionNotDefinedException and DriverNotSpecifiedException now implement DatabaseException. SchemaDefinitionException no longer extends SchemaException and extends \RuntimeException instead. New Drupal\Core\Database\Exception\SchemaTableDoesNotExistException (extends SchemaObjectDoesNotExistException) and SchemaTableAlreadyExistsException (extends SchemaObjectExistsException) are thrown by Schema::createTable(), introspectIndexSchema() and the MySQL renameTable(). The MySQL handler also maps error codes 1050, 1051 and 1146 to them. The new exceptions extend the old ones, so existing catch blocks keep working.

In the core ExceptionHandler, handleStatementException() and handleExecutionException() now delegate to a new protected rethrowNormalizedException() that builds SqlExecutionInfo, so SQL and placeholders are available on the exception. The MySQL, pgsql and SQLite handlers follow the same pattern, so statement-level errors are normalized on every driver. Connection::getDriverClass() now throws \InvalidArgumentException instead of InvalidQueryException for the unsupported legacy class lookup. TransactionExplicitCommitNotAllowedException is deprecated in drupal:12.1.0 and removed in drupal:13.0.0, with a trigger_error() on load.

Upgrade

Code that parses database exception messages should not rely on the old format (message: sql; Array (...)). Read the SQL and placeholders from the new property instead:

try {
  $connection->query($sql, $args);
}
catch (\Drupal\Core\Database\DatabaseExceptionWrapper $e) {
  $sql = $e->info?->sqlQuery;
  $placeholders = $e->info?->placeholders;
}

Stop referencing TransactionExplicitCommitNotAllowedException. Contrib database drivers should have their exception handlers throw SchemaTableDoesNotExistException and SchemaTableAlreadyExistsException and pass a SqlExecutionInfo to the wrapper exceptions. The issue mentions two change records for these points, but I did not read them.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: September 11, 2026
  • Committed: November 26, 2026 (2 months later)

Key contributors

  • mondrake
  • dcam
  • daffie (Finalist)

  • catch (Tag1 Consulting)

item.title: #3328425: CKEditor 5 balloons invisible when CKEditor 5 is used inside a modal
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Major bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 12 files, +322/−196 · php +297/−183 · yml +14/−7 · css +11/−6
  • Diff: 75a5600
  • Discussion: #3328425 · 32 contributors · 96 comments
  • Followers: 53
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 32 contributors

Summary

CKEditor 5 balloons, such as the link dialog opened from the toolbar, are now visible when the editor is inside a modal dialog. Before, the balloon could render behind the dialog, so links could not be added in a CKEditor 5 field inside a modal, for example a media caption or a Layout Builder or Paragraphs modal. The fix is in CSS only.

Impact

Affects front-end developers.

  • Theme change: ckeditor5.dialog.fix.css now applies to every .ck-body-wrapper and raises --ck-z-panel above jQuery UI dialogs, so themes or modules carrying their own z-index overrides for CKEditor 5 balloons can drop them.

Technical details

The balloon z-index (1000) was below the jQuery UI dialog (1260). The earlier fix from #3274937 used the selector .ui-dialog ~ .ck-body-wrapper, which only matches when .ck-body-wrapper comes after the dialog in the DOM. CKEditor 5 appends one shared body wrapper when the first editor is created. If an editor already exists on the page before the dialog opens, the wrapper comes first and the rule does not match.

In core/modules/ckeditor5/css/ckeditor5.dialog.fix.css the selector is now plain .ck-body-wrapper. It sets --ck-z-panel: calc(var(--ck-z-default) + 1261). Thread comments say 1262 is needed so a balloon works in a modal opened from within another modal. It also redeclares --ck-layer-panel, --ck-layer-panel-above and --ck-layer-panel-below on the wrapper. The CSS comment says CKEditor 5 49.0.0 and later resolves these on :root, so they would not pick up the override otherwise.

The change landed in two attempts. The first commit was reverted because its own new test failed on main. The second commit added the layer variables. The patch adds a ckeditor5_test.dialog_with_editor route and a CKEditor5DialogTestForm to the ckeditor5_test module. It also adds testBalloonVisibleInDialogOpenedAfterEditor() to CKEditor5DialogTest. That test checks that the balloon is the topmost element at its centre point, using the default_admin theme because Stark does not raise dialog z-index.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: December 20, 2022
  • First commit: November 24, 2026 (3 years later)
  • Last commit: November 26, 2026 (1 day and 3 commits later)

Key contributors

  • cedewey (DevCollaborative, LLC)
  • mherchel
  • hudri (webtourismus.at)
  • realityloop
  • scott_euser (Soapbox)
  • cecrs
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • nod_ (Très Bien Tech)
  • arousseau
  • lauriii (Acquia)
  • quietone (PreviousNext)

Collaboration

The issue ran from 2022 to 2026. mherchel traced the cause to DOM order and the z-index values. scott_euser later reworked the MR for current CKEditor 5 variable names and tested a modal inside a modal, which showed the value had to be one higher than first proposed. nod_ asked for a regression test, and scott_euser said it was hard to test z-index visibility. A test using elementFromPoint was added before commit.

item.title: #3122231: Singular variant for plural string must contain @count, otherwise Drupal displays wrong data for untranslated strings
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal bug report
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 65 files, +227/−162 · php +198/−135 · js +22/−20 · yml +6/−6 · twig +1/−1
  • Diff: 0387fb9
  • Discussion: #3122231 · 11 contributors · 60 comments
  • Followers: 17
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 11 contributors

Summary

The documented rule for plural strings has flipped. The singular form must now contain @count, not a literal "1" or "one". In many languages the first plural form is also used for counts other than 1 (for example 21 in Russian or 0 in French), so an untranslated "1 day" singular displays the wrong number. A singular like "1 minute" can also clash with a standalone "1 minute" string in a .po file and break msgfmt -c. Core's own plural strings were updated to follow the new rule. Custom and contrib code with singulars like '1 item' should switch to '@count item'.

Impact

No upgrade or configuration changes required.

Technical details

The docs for the $singular parameter were rewritten in TranslationInterface::formatPlural(), TranslationManager, PluralTranslatableMarkup::__construct() and Drupal.formatPlural() in drupal.js. They now say not to put "1" or "one" in the string and to always use @count. The old statement that @count is replaced "for the plural cases" only was removed, since it is replaced in both forms. Examples in core/lib/Drupal/Core/Form/form.inc-style docblocks and the formatPlural() examples now use '@count comment'.

The patch also converts core singulars from "1 ..." or "One ..." to @count .... This covers the locale import and update messages, BundleEntityDeleteForm, UserLoginForm, the block and workspace messages, the file field cardinality description, ByteSizeMarkup, and the format_plural_string value in two shipped views YAML files (@count + delimiter + @count). Tests and the JS extraction fixture were adjusted, for example "One translation file imported" is now asserted as "1 translation file imported". Because the singular is the msgid of a plural entry in a .po file, these source strings changed, so existing translations of them may no longer match. No runtime check or deprecation was added for singulars lacking @count. A coding standards or static analysis check was discussed as a follow-up. Related: #3631439, #1788008, #2273889.

Upgrade

Use @count in the singular string in your own code:

// Before
\Drupal::translation()->formatPlural($count, '1 comment', '@count comments');
// After
\Drupal::translation()->formatPlural($count, '@count comment', '@count comments');

Drupal.formatPlural(count, '@count something', '@count somethings');

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: March 25, 2020
  • Committed: November 25, 2026 (6 years later)

Key contributors

  • niklan
  • andypost (Skilld)
  • kunalgautam (Material)
  • larowlan (PreviousNext)
  • dww (TEN7)
  • d34dman (Factorial.io)
  • gábor hojtsy (Acquia)
  • xjm (xjm)
  • alexpott (Acro Commerce)
  • godotislate
  • longwave (Full Fat Things)

Collaboration

Gábor Hojtsy revived the issue and widened it beyond documentation. He gathered how i18next, WordPress and Django put the count in the singular, and listed the APIs that can produce plural strings. Alexpott reviewed every @count instance in core and found missed conversions, such as those in time-diff.js and BatchUserAction. Godotislate found missed test and YAML strings before committing, then wrote the backports to 12.0.x, 11.x and 11.5.x.

item.title: #3641267: Update Twig to v3.31.1
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 10.6.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +20/−25 · lock +17/−17 · php +2/−7 · json +1/−1
  • Diff: 1dec2b8
  • Discussion: #3641267 · 5 contributors · 34 comments
  • Followers: 6
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Drupal core now requires and locks Twig 3.31.1 (and twig/html-extra 3.31.1), picking up fixes for newly published Twig CVEs. The update was also committed to the 12.0.x, 11.x, 11.5.x, 11.4.x, 11.3.x and 10.6.x branches. Sites should update to a core release containing it, or otherwise run composer update twig/twig so composer audit stops reporting the advisories.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Security: Updates Twig to v3.31.1 to address newly released Twig CVEs (the issue flags them via composer audit).
  • API change: Core's Twig loader addPath() gains a third parameter bool $check = TRUE on main, matching Twig's FilesystemLoader; subclasses overriding it need a compatible signature.

Technical details

The commit bumps the twig/twig constraint from ^3.28.0 to ^3.31.1 in core's composer.json, and updates composer.lock (twig/twig from v3.30.0 to v3.31.1, twig/html-extra from v3.29.0 to v3.31.1). The issue states lockfiles and core-recommended need the update before further security releases on all supported branches.

Twig 3.31 adds a bool $check argument to FilesystemLoader::addPath(). Core's Twig loader overrides that method, so on main its signature becomes addPath(string $path, string $namespace = self::MAIN_NAMESPACE, bool $check = TRUE): void, and the docblock is replaced with {@inheritdoc}. In the thread, the concern was that making this a required signature change could disrupt contrib or custom subclasses on production branches; for 11.4.x the MR was reworked to use Twig's commented-out parameter form (/* , bool $check = true */) with deprecation ignores, while 11.5.x keeps the new parameter. I only read the main diff, so the exact backport forms on other branches are not verified here.

Upgrade

If you extend the core Twig loader and override addPath(), update the signature on main/12.0.x:

public function addPath(string $path, string $namespace = self::MAIN_NAMESPACE, bool $check = TRUE): void {

Sites using their own lockfile should run composer update twig/twig twig/html-extra.

  • Opened: November 24, 2026
  • Committed: November 24, 2026

item.title: #2448545: Modernize form select option helpers
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 3 files, +126/−60 · php +126/−60
  • Diff: ca18eda
  • Discussion: #2448545 · 48 contributors · 185 comments
  • Followers: 53

Summary

The two remaining option helper functions in form.inc are deprecated. form_select_options() now has a class-based replacement, and form_get_options(), which core does not use, is deprecated with no replacement. Both will be removed in Drupal 13. Contrib and custom code that calls either function will emit deprecation notices.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: form_select_options() deprecated in favour of \Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions::process(); form_get_options() deprecated with no replacement, both removed in drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New final class \Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions with static process() method.

Technical details

The logic of form_select_options() moved unchanged into the new final class Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions as FormSelectOptions::process(array $element, $choices = NULL): array. The class has a private constructor and is not meant to be instantiated or extended. The old function now calls trigger_error() with E_USER_DEPRECATED and delegates to process(). Core's own caller, the select preprocess in ElementInfoManager-adjacent theme preprocess code (preprocessSelect()), now calls FormSelectOptions::process() directly. The docblocks were moved as they were, with improvements left to the follow-up #3548829.

form_get_options() only gets a deprecation notice and trigger, with no replacement. One small difference in the moved code: the empty-option check for multiple selects changed from $key == '_none' to $key === '_none'. Since $key is already cast to a string, behaviour should be the same. Replacing the hard-coded '_none' with a constant was split into #3548830. The earlier broader approach, which introduced an options constant, was dropped to reduce scope.

Upgrade

Replace calls to the deprecated function:

// Before.
$options = form_select_options($element);
// After.
use Drupal\Core\Form\FormSelectOptions;
$options = FormSelectOptions::process($element);

form_get_options() has no replacement; stop using it.

item.title: #3249027: RoleAccessCheck returns Allowed if user has no role
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 2 files, +31/−15 · php +31/−15
  • Diff: 3a0ae0d
  • Discussion: #3249027 · 16 contributors · 59 comments
  • Followers: 18
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 16 contributors

Summary

The _role route access check now explicitly denies access when an account has no roles at all. Core accounts always carry at least the anonymous or authenticated role, so ordinary sites see no change. The guard protects against future changes, such as a different default for getRoles(), or custom account objects that return no roles.

Impact

Affects site owners.

  • Security: RoleAccessCheck now returns forbidden for any account with no roles, a defensive guard with no known exploit in current core.

Technical details

\Drupal\user\Access\RoleAccessCheck::access() now calls $account->getRoles() once, and if the result is empty returns AccessResult::forbidden('No user roles found.') before parsing the _role requirement. Previously an empty role list on a _role route fell through to AccessResult::neutral() with the user.roles cache context. The same $roles variable is reused in the array_diff() (comma, AND) and array_intersect() (plus, OR) branches. The forbidden result carries no user.roles cache context.

Because forbidden wins over allowed when access results are combined, an account without roles is now denied outright, where before another access checker could still grant access. The thread established that the bug was not reproducible in current core: an empty array already led to neutral. The change is a guard against future changes. RoleAccessCheckTest gains a $forbidden_accounts data provider argument covering $account_none (empty roles) and $account_null (NULL roles).

item.title: #3437608: Add validation constraints to system.performance
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: main
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 11 files, +466/−19 · php +386/−5 · yml +80/−14
  • Diff: ab043e9
  • Discussion: #3437608 · 11 contributors · 79 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 11 contributors

Summary

The system.performance config is now fully validatable. Page cache max age must be an integer between 0 and 31536000 seconds. When Fast 404 is enabled, its paths and exclude_paths must be valid regular expressions and its html must be a valid HTML document, and all three keys are required. When Fast 404 is disabled, those keys may be omitted, but if present they are still validated. Core also gains reusable Html and ValidRegex constraints and matching schema types that contrib and custom config schemas can use.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: system.performance is now FullyValidatable; cache.page.max_age must be 0 to 31536000, and fast_404 paths, exclude_paths and html are validated and required when fast_404.enabled is true.
  • New API: New Html (mode fragment or document) and ValidRegex validation constraints, and new html_fragment, html_document and regex config schema data types.

Technical details

core.data_types.schema.yml gains three types: regex (constraint ValidRegex), html_fragment (Html with mode: fragment) and html_document (Html with mode: document). The constraints live in Drupal\Core\Validation\Plugin\Validation\Constraint as HtmlConstraint/HtmlConstraintValidator and ValidRegexConstraint/ValidRegexConstraintValidator. They sit in core's Validation namespace rather than a component, to avoid a new dependency from the Utility component. HtmlConstraint throws an InvalidArgumentException for any mode other than fragment or document; the validator parses with Masterminds\HTML5 and adds each parser error as a violation, and ignores NULL. ValidRegexConstraintValidator checks @preg_match($value, "") !== FALSE and reports the preg_last_error_msg() text in the violation.

In system.schema.yml, cache.page.max_age gets a Range of 0 to 31536000, matching PerformanceForm::buildForm(). fast_404 is now a dynamic type system.performance.fast_404.[enabled], resolving to system.performance.fast_404.1 (enabled: paths, exclude_paths, html required) or system.performance.fast_404.0 (disabled: the same keys with requiredKey: false), both extending system.performance.fast_404.*. Consequently, enabling Fast 404 without those keys fails with SchemaIncompleteException on save. Fast404Test and CommandsTest were adjusted accordingly (the latter now calls installConfig(['system'])). Coverage of the HTML validator is questioned in follow-up #3639758.

Upgrade

Custom schemas can reuse the new types:

my_module.settings:
  type: config_object
  mapping:
    pattern:
      type: regex
      label: 'Regular expression'
    page_html:
      type: html_document
      label: 'HTML page'

Code that enables fast_404 in system.performance programmatically must also set paths, exclude_paths and html.

Contribution

Timeline

  • Opened: April 2, 2024

item.title: #3622391: Use tagged iterators in CacheTagsInvalidator
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 12.0.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 4 files, +168/−21 · php +167/−17 · yml +1/−4
  • Diff: af2ff7c
  • Discussion: #3622391 · 7 contributors · 21 comments
  • Followers: 12
  • AI disclosures: 1 of 7 contributors

Summary

The cache tags invalidator no longer instantiates every cache tag invalidator service and every cache bin when it is built. They are loaded lazily, only when tags are actually invalidated. This removes a source of circular service references (for example a logger that reads config in its constructor, combined with a config override that triggers plugin discovery), and avoids constructing services that are never needed on a request. Sites or modules that subclass CacheTagsInvalidator or replace the cache_tags.invalidator service may need updating.

Impact

Affects module maintainers and site owners.

  • Config change: cache_tags.invalidator service definition now uses !tagged_iterator arguments instead of service_collector tags.
  • API change: CacheTagsInvalidator has a new constructor taking iterable $invalidators, $bins and $memoryBins; the $invalidators and $bins properties are now iterable.

Technical details

The cache_tags.invalidator service in core.services.yml dropped the three service_collector tags (addInvalidator for cache_tags_invalidator, addBin for cache.bin and cache.bin.memory). It now passes !tagged_iterator cache_tags_invalidator, !tagged_iterator cache.bin and !tagged_iterator cache.bin.memory as constructor arguments. CacheTagsInvalidator gained a constructor with promoted protected iterable $invalidators = [], $bins = [] and $memoryBins = [].

Because tagged iterators now include every service with the cache.bin tags, not just those implementing the invalidator interface, invalidateTags() checks instanceof CacheTagsInvalidatorInterface for each bin before calling it. addInvalidator() and addBin() still work: they rebuild the property as an array spreading the existing iterable plus the new item, so runtime additions and repeated iteration are supported. Operations such as resetChecksums() and purge() only touch the invalidators, not the bins. New kernel test CacheTagsInvalidatorTest asserts the tagged services are not initialized until invalidateTags() is called.

The change was committed to main and 12.0.x. The committer preferred breaking subclasses in 12.0.x rather than later. Related: #3612284 (circular reference discovered in the raven module), #3632318.

Upgrade

If you extend CacheTagsInvalidator with your own constructor, pass the new arguments to the parent constructor:

public function __construct(
  protected iterable $invalidators = [],
  protected iterable $bins = [],
  protected iterable $memoryBins = [],
) {}

If you define a replacement service, supply the same tagged iterators as core does:

cache_tags.invalidator:
  class: Drupal\Core\Cache\CacheTagsInvalidator
  arguments: [!tagged_iterator cache_tags_invalidator, !tagged_iterator cache.bin, !tagged_iterator cache.bin.memory]

Subclasses with no constructor of their own need no change. addInvalidator() and addBin() remain available.

item.title: #3623380: Create OOP replacement for hook_install_tasks and hook_install_tasks_alter
item.description:
• Project: Drupal Core
  • Type: Normal task
  • Version: 11.5.x-dev
  • Status: Fixed
  • Changes: 8 files, +372/−21 · php +367/−21 · yml +5
  • Diff: 4f9558d
  • Discussion: #3623380 · 5 contributors · 33 comments
  • Followers: 8
  • AI disclosures: 0 of 5 contributors

Summary

Installation profiles can now provide their custom install tasks and task alterations through a class instead of hook_install_tasks() and hook_install_tasks_alter() in the .profile file. This removes one of the remaining reasons profiles need a procedural .profile file. The old procedural hooks still work but now trigger deprecation errors.

Impact

Affects module maintainers.

  • Deprecation: Procedural hook_install_tasks() and hook_install_tasks_alter() are deprecated in drupal:11.5.0 and removed from drupal:13.0.0.
  • New API: New \Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface with getTasks(array &$install_state): array and alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state): void.

Technical details

A profile adds a class in src/Install/Tasks/ (namespace Drupal\PROFILE_NAME\Install\Tasks) that implements \Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface. getTasks(array &$install_state) replaces hook_install_tasks() and alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state) replaces hook_install_tasks_alter(). The class is created through \Drupal::classResolver(), so it can implement ContainerInjectionInterface. Only core services can safely be injected, because this runs before the install is complete.

In install.core.inc, install_tasks() calls the new install_get_tasks() and install_alter_tasks() helpers (both @internal). The procedural PROFILE_install_tasks() and PROFILE_install_tasks_alter() are only called when no OOP implementation supplied tasks (for getTasks) or exists (for alter). When the procedural fallback runs, it triggers an E_USER_DEPRECATED error pointing to https://www.drupal.org/node/3623397. The profile file is still loaded before alter(), so the class can rely on functions defined there.

The directory scan that install_check_class_requirements() used to find Install/Requirements classes was extracted into install_get_fixed_class_name(), which now serves both lookups. It require_onces each PHP file in the directory and keeps the class name of the last file it finds, so keep one class per Install/Tasks directory. The hook docs in core.api.php were updated with the @deprecated notes. Follow-up #3630429 is about changing the doc wording on state versus key value expirable.

Upgrade

Move the procedural hooks into a class, for example src/Install/Tasks/MyProfileTasks.php:

namespace Drupal\myprofile\Install\Tasks;

use Drupal\Core\Extension\Install\TasksInterface;

class MyProfileTasks implements TasksInterface {

  public function getTasks(array &$install_state): array {
    // Return what myprofile_install_tasks() returned.
    return [];
  }

  public function alter(array &$tasks, array $install_state): void {
    // Body of myprofile_install_tasks_alter().
  }

}

Then remove myprofile_install_tasks() and myprofile_install_tasks_alter() from the .profile file. If the class exists, the procedural versions are ignored.
